target_customer: First time retail investors in India who want direct mutual funds without distributor commissions
problem: Indian retail investors paid distributor commissions and found mutual fund investing confusing, so few started.
business_model: Consumer investing app charging a basic transaction fee, later a premium subscription
product_category: Fintech, direct mutual fund investing app

founders.name: Ankush Singh
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2017 says the founders came from various banking backgrounds without naming employers. A secondary summary names Nomura, not confirmed on an opened source.

founders.name: Nikhil Satya Mantha
founders.background_notes: Quoted by TechCrunch describing the aim as the Vanguard for India.

founders.name: Kunal Sangwan
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder and CTO on the YC page and named by TechCrunch.

exit.reason: No public reason; users were told by email on 2025-05-30 that the app would close within about 30 days

competitors.name: Zerodha Coin
competitors.what: Direct mutual fund platform with zero fund commissions

competitors.name: Robinhood
competitors.what: US commission free investing app that TechCrunch cites as a comparable, with a different flow for India

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile app on top of regulated mutual fund rails and registrar integrations, standard engineering with compliance steps.

defensibility.rationale: Direct plans are open to any app, TechCrunch notes other startups and large fund houses could compete, and a later secondary source says better funded rivals copied the wedge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Zerodha launched Coin months before the batch. Later rivals such as Groww and Kuvera are named as winners by a secondary source, not dated here.

market_need_then: TechCrunch 2017 describes first time investors in India needing a simple route to mutual funds. A 2020 Business Today profile, later than founding, reports over 100,000 users.

branding.domain_note: Operated at piggy.co.in, a country domain, not piggy.com.

brand_strength.rationale: Piggy had press from TechCrunch and Business Today, but the piggy bank name is shared by other fintech brands such as PiggyVest, and no source shows brand driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Piggy launched a commission free direct mutual fund app in India after YC in 2017 and later reported over 100,000 users and about $170M in assets in 2020. External funding stayed tiny, about $19,900 in 2016 and a $25,000 Flipkart Leap grant in 2021, per aggregators. Rivals with more capital copied the zero commission wedge, and Piggy told users on 2025-05-30 it would close within about 30 days, with no stated reason. Competition and undercapitalization come from one secondary site and are the best available reading, not a company statement.
notes: piggy.co.in could not be fetched (host not resolvable from this session), so the site is treated as unreachable. Shutdown date and cause rest on a secondary dead startup site and search summaries; no primary shutdown source was opened. The 2016 angel round of 19900 rests on that single site. The Flipkart Leap grant of 25000 is reported by CB Insights and Inc42; CB Insights totals 30000 over three rounds while the dead startups site says about 162000 over four rounds, so the history is incomplete and conflicting. Arab Angel Fund and VentureSouq are listed by CB Insights without round details and are not recorded. Yearly user and AUM figures are from 2020, after founding.
